summary: Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2001) under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying under G. Raj. She held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend A. van Nooten is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2007).

Barend Faddegon worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University (PhD) under Jacob Samuel Speyer, Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern, later serving as professor at Amsterdam (1908–1944).

Barend J. ter Haar works in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher and studied under Susan Naquin, holding posts at Heidelberg (~1994–2000), Leiden (~2000–2013), and Hamburg (~2018).

Barend Jan Terwiel specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University (PhD), later holding posts at ANU, the University of Munich (~1988–1992), and the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, the University of Southern California (MD), and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He held posts at the University of Washington (1985–1989) and the University of Hong Kong.

Barry Tse works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Federation University Australia, the University of Queensland, the University of Liverpool, and James Cook University Singapore (PhD), where he taught (2022–2026) before joining the University of Newcastle in 2026.

Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Liaoning University and Ghent University (PhD 1990–1994) under Charles Willemen, and was appointed associate professor at Ghent University in 1990.

Barthold Georg Niebuhr was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Kiel University (~1794–1796). He later held chairs at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1816) and the University of Bonn (~1823–1831).
Basil Gould was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at New College and the University of Oxford (~1902–1906) before joining the Indian Civil Service in 1907.

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve worked in linguistics. He studied at Princeton, Bonn under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and Göttingen (Dr. phil.) under Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He served as professor at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Batakrishna Ghosh was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Hanns Oertel (~1930–1935). He held posts as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bazar Baradiin was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied and taught at Saint Petersburg State University. He later headed the Buryat Scientific Center (~1922–1929) and the Buryat State Pedagogical Institute (1932–1935).

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University, was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley (~1987–1989), and became associate professor at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989).

Beatrice Erskine Lane worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer, and at Columbia University. In 1921, she took up a post at Otani University.

Beatrix Pfleiderer worked in Indology. She studied at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University, holding posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (1971–1975), Heidelberg (1973–1976), and the University of Hamburg (from 1982).
Bedika Rai works in Buddhist studies. She held posts as assistant professor at Salesian College (2010–2019) and Kalipada Ghosh Tarai Mahavidyalaya (2019).

Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at the University of Vienna (PhD 1897–1901) and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1905) and Charles University as professor (1919).
Bedřich Votýpka was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (1885–1892) under Josef Zubatý. He worked as a gymnasium professor at Gymnázium Benešov.

Beier Wang works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Wang studied at the University of Toronto, the University of Hong Kong, and the University of Leipzig (PhD 2021), where Wang served as a research assistant (2022–2025).
